diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Continuous controllers index a per-channel value array; controllers 98-101 (NRPN and RPN data entry) switch the reader into a two-byte parameter-number mode with its own state machine; controllers 120-127 are mode messages (all sound off, reset all controllers, local control, all notes off, omni off/on, mono/poly) that reset state rather than store a value. Emitting only 1, 7, 10 and 64 reaches none of that.
diversity_axes.notes: Sweep 0-127 with deliberate weight on the RPN/NRPN group and the mode-message group, and vary the value byte across its full span too, including 0 and 127.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Bitmask is the data-byte rule only; all 128 program numbers stay free. This message carries ONE data byte, not two, so its size must not be normalised to match the other channel messages.
diversity_axes.why: The program number selects an instrument patch, which readers use to index patch tables and to decide drum-versus-melodic handling on channel 9.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Patch lookup and validation against the loaded sound set, the channel-9 percussion special case, and any bank-select interaction with controllers 0 and 32. Program 0 and 127 reach the ends of the patch table.
diversity_axes.notes: Span 0-127 with weight on both boundaries, and combine with bank-select controller changes so the reader's bank-plus-program resolution path is reached.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Bitmask is the data-byte rule only; both bytes stay free over 0-127. The pair forms a 14-bit signed value, and the least-significant byte comes FIRST - reversing the order is a framing error, not a diversity choice.
diversity_axes.why: The combined 14-bit bend value is sign-extended, scaled by the per-channel bend range and compared against the centre position, so its extremes and its centre take different paths.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The bend handler's two-byte reassembly (LSB then MSB), the sign test at the top of the 14-bit range, the centre-value fast path, and the range-scaling multiply. Emitting only centre values leaves the sign and scaling paths unexecuted; emitting only extremes leaves the centre fast path unexecuted.
diversity_axes.notes: Cover the pair at 0x00 0x00 (minimum), 0x00 0x40 (centre), 0x7F 0x7F (maximum) and freely in between, always writing the low byte first.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Emit the whole legal byte span 0x00-0x7F, not just the 18 values the template names. Unassigned and reserved types are legal: SMF requires readers to skip an unknown meta event by length, and that skip path is a real branch that named types never reach.
diversity_axes.why: The meta type byte drives a second-level dispatch inside the meta arm, and each arm has its own payload layout.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Thirteen named arms with distinct layouts - sequence number (two forms, length 0 and length 2), eight text arms, channel prefix, port, end of track (empty), tempo (3-byte big-endian), SMPTE offset (5 bytes), time signature (4 bytes), key signature (2 bytes) - plus the length-delimited skip arm for every unrecognised type. Only emitting tempo and end of track reaches three of those.
diversity_axes.notes: Include the reserved gaps 0x0A-0x1F, 0x22-0x2E, 0x30-0x46, 0x48-0x50, 0x52-0x57 and 0x5A-0x7E with a VLQ length and that many payload bytes, and emit META_SEQUENCE_NUM (0x00) in both its length-0 and length-2 forms.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A on the VALUE - it must equal the number of payload bytes emitted - but the payload SIZE is a free choice for the eight variable-length meta types. Never pin the length to a few small constants so that precomputed payloads can be reused; build the payload, count it, then write the count.
diversity_axes.why: This quantity is the array bound for the payload, and text and sequencer-specific meta events are where most of a file's byte volume can legitimately come from.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The payload read of the selected meta arm, the allocation sized by this count, and the skip-by-length path for unknown types. A zero length takes the empty-payload branch, which readers handle separately from a non-empty one; a multi-byte length additionally exercises the VLQ decode a second time inside the same event.
diversity_axes.notes: Eight types have lengths fixed by the specification and are recorded in `dependencies` (0x00 -> 0 or 2, 0x20 -> 1, 0x21 -> 1, 0x2F -> 0, 0x51 -> 3, 0x54 -> 5, 0x58 -> 4, 0x59 -> 2). Every other type has a free length, bounded only by the output_budget in `structure`.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Completely free: the full 16-bit big-endian span, including 0. No value set, no minimum, no maximum.
diversity_axes.why: The sequence number is used for pattern selection and matching in format 2 files, so its value decides which track a reader pairs with which pattern.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The pattern-selection and track-matching logic of format 2 playback, plus the two-byte big-endian read itself. In formats 0 and 1 readers record it without acting on it, so the value still parses.
diversity_axes.notes: Emit the event both with length 2 and a value, and with length 0 and no payload at all - those are two distinct arms of the same type byte. In format 2 files give each track a different number so the matching logic has something to distinguish.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Completely free in both length and byte content. These are the only meta payloads interpreted as characters rather than numbers, and a length of zero is legal - do not require non-empty text and do not restrict the alphabet.
diversity_axes.why: Text payload length and content drive string handling, encoding conversion and line splitting in readers, and the eight text types are dispatched separately rather than sharing one handler.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Per-type text handling (some readers treat lyrics and markers specially, splitting on newlines or synchronising them to events), the allocation and copy sized by meta_event.m_length, the empty-payload branch when the length is 0, and any character-encoding conversion applied to bytes with bit 7 set. A corpus of only short ASCII strings reaches the allocation fast path and nothing else.
diversity_axes.notes: Cover every one of the eight text types, since readers often dispatch per type. Vary the length across 0, 1, a few bytes and a few hundred, and vary the content across printable ASCII, high-bit bytes 0x80-0xFF, embedded NUL, CR and LF and other control characters, and multi-byte UTF-8 sequences. Total payload bytes are bounded by the output_budget in `structure`, never by narrowing this field.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Completely free: the full byte span for both fields. Values above 15 are outside the documented channel range but no reader refuses a file over them, so they stay legal for generation purposes.
diversity_axes.why: The channel prefix re-attributes the channel of the sysex and meta events that follow it, and the port selects an output device, so both change which state a reader writes to without changing any length or framing.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The channel-attribution state that readers apply to subsequent sysex and meta events until the next prefix or the end of the track, and the port/device selection path. Emitting neither leaves the default-channel path as the only one ever taken.
diversity_axes.notes: Each is exactly one byte, so meta_event.m_length must encode 1. Place a prefix before some sysex events so the attribution logic has something to act on, and vary the port value across its span including 0.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Completely free: the full 24-bit span, including 0. Do not restrict it to conventional tempos - a zero or tiny value reaches a division path that a mid-range value never does.
diversity_axes.why: This is the divisor that converts ticks into real time, so its value drives tempo arithmetic and any tempo-change tracking across the file.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The tempo-to-tick division (with its zero-divisor guard in readers that have one), the tempo-map update when the value changes mid-track, and the SMPTE-mode path where this field is ignored entirely in favour of the division. Conventional values only reach the interior of the division.
diversity_axes.notes: Three bytes, big-endian, declared as a 24-bit bitfield; meta_event.m_length must encode 3. Emit several tempo changes within a track so the tempo-map update path runs more than once, and include small values, 0, and values near 0xFFFFFF.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Completely free: the full byte span of all five SMPTE-offset fields, including values outside the documented hour/minute/second/frame ranges. No reader refuses a file over an impossible timecode, so none of these bytes may be narrowed.
diversity_axes.why: The five bytes are split, validated and recombined into a start timecode, so their values move the reader through the SMPTE conversion arithmetic.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The SMPTE start-time assembly (hours with its top two bits reserved for the drop-frame and colour-frame flags, minutes, seconds, frames, and fractional frames in hundredths), the frames-per-second conversion, and the drop-frame compensation path that only runs when the flag bits are set. This whole area is dead code unless the file also uses a negative MidiHeader.m_tickdiv.
diversity_axes.notes: Exactly five bytes, so meta_event.m_length must encode 5. Pair these events with an SMPTE-mode division so the reader's timecode path is actually taken, and set the reserved top bits of the hour byte sometimes to reach the drop-frame and colour-frame handling.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Completely free: the full byte span of all four time-signature bytes, including 0. The denominator byte is a shift exponent and the 32nd-note byte is a multiplier, so unusual values reach arithmetic that conventional ones do not - which is a reason to leave them free, not to bound them.
diversity_axes.why: These four bytes drive bar-length and metronome arithmetic, and the denominator is applied as a power-of-two shift.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The bar-line and beat-length computation (numerator times the shifted denominator), the metronome click interval, the 32nd-note grid multiplier, and any validation or default substitution a reader applies to an out-of-range exponent. Conventional 4/4 values only ever take the interior of that arithmetic.
diversity_axes.notes: Exactly four bytes, so meta_event.m_length must encode 4. Note that the stored denominator is log2 of the real denominator (2 means a quarter note), which is a format rule to encode correctly - not a reason to bound the byte to 0-3.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Completely free: the full SIGNED byte span of both key-signature bytes. The -7..+7 span and the two major/minor values are the specification's convention, not a gate, and recording them as a bound would be exactly the GIF mistake.
diversity_axes.why: The pair selects a key name, so it drives any key lookup or transposition table a reader has, and it is one of the few signed fields in the format.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The key-name lookup indexed by the signed offset, taking both the flat and the sharp side of the table, and the major/minor selection including any default or error branch for an unexpected quality value. Note the field is declared `char`, which is signed in 010 Editor, so negative offsets are the two's-complement bytes 0xF9-0xFF.
diversity_axes.notes: Exactly two bytes, so meta_event.m_length must encode 2. Emit offsets on both sides of zero and both quality values, and let some files carry offsets outside -7..+7 to reach a reader's out-of-range handling.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Completely free in both length and content: this is the fallback payload for every meta type the template does not name, including META_SEQUENCER_EVENT (0x7F) and all unassigned types.
diversity_axes.why: Reaching this array at all requires emitting meta types that a naive generator would skip as 'undefined', and the skip-unknown path is one of the few branches that only unusual files can enter.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The unknown-meta skip-by-length path, the allocation and copy for a payload of arbitrary size, and for type 0x7F the vendor-specific dispatch that reads a manufacturer ID from the first bytes. Named meta types never reach any of it.
diversity_axes.notes: Any byte 0x00-0xFF is legal because the run is length-delimited. For type 0x7F the payload conventionally starts with a manufacturer ID, but readers do not require it, so both forms are worth emitting. Total bytes are bounded by the output_budget in `structure`.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A on the VALUE - it must equal the number of sysex payload bytes emitted - but the payload size is a free choice. Never pin it to a few small constants so a fixed set of precomputed sysex blobs can be reused; build the payload, count its bytes, then write the count. This field is named in sysex_event.m_message's derives_from, so it must not be narrowed to suit any payload.
diversity_axes.why: It is the array bound of the sysex payload and the only thing that tells a reader where the exclusive message ends.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The sysex payload read and the allocation sized by this count, the VLQ decode inside the event, and the zero-length case where the payload is empty. A disagreement with the bytes present shifts every later event and breaks the track length check.
diversity_axes.notes: A length of 0 is legal and produces an empty sysex payload. Whether the terminating 0xF7 is counted inside the length is the long-standing SMF ambiguity; the dominant convention counts it in and readers are expected to accept both.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A on the FRAMING (status 0xF0 or 0xF7, then a VLQ length, then exactly that many payload bytes; nothing inside the payload may be re-interpreted as a status byte). The CONTENT is completely free: any byte 0x00-0xFF at any length, including 0.
diversity_axes.why: Exclusive messages are the format's only escape hatch to vendor-defined data, and both status forms take this payload path with different framing rules.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The sysex payload read bounded by sysex_event.m_length, the manufacturer-ID dispatch for recognised IDs, the 0xF7 escape form where the payload is arbitrary bytes that must not be re-framed as events, and the length-0 case. A corpus that omits sysex entirely, or emits only 0xF0 with a fixed small payload, reaches almost none of this.
diversity_axes.notes: Emit both the 0xF0 form (conventionally ending in 0xF7 inside the payload) and the 0xF7 escape form (payload arbitrary, no 0xF7 required). The escape form is the correct way to carry the forbidden statuses 0xF1-0xF6 and 0xF8-0xFE, which lets a reader's system-common and real-time handling be reached without breaking the track framing.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A on the VALUE - it must equal the byte count of the event run that follows, delta times, statuses and payloads all included - but the length of that run is a free choice per track. Never cap tracks at a fixed byte count so one precomputed event blob can be reused; emit the events, count the bytes, then write the count.
diversity_axes.why: It is the sole delimiter of the event run: it tells the reader where the track ends, where the next MTrk begins, and whether the file's total length is trustworthy.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The track-boundary arithmetic, the end-of-run condition of the event loop, the chunk walk to the next MTrk magic, and the reader's whole-file length check. An empty or very short track takes the loop's immediate-exit path; a long track drives the loop, the running-status state and the tick accumulator many times over. A value that disagrees with the emitted bytes desynchronises every later event.
diversity_axes.notes: Vary track lengths widely across the corpus - from a track holding only an end-of-track event to tracks of many kilobytes - and make the per-track lengths unequal so the chunk walk cannot succeed by accident.

diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A on the COUNT relationship: it must equal MidiHeader.m_ntracks exactly, and every track must be fully written. The number of tracks and their event content are free choices bounded only by the output_budget below, so they may not be narrowed to keep files small.
diversity_axes.why: This is the file's only repeating top-level structure, and its repetition count is what makes the chunk walk and the whole-file length check meaningful.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The chunk iteration loop with its per-iteration magic check and length read, per-track state allocation and reset, the running-status reset that happens at each track boundary, and the final whole-file length assertion. Zero tracks exits the loop immediately; many tracks of unequal length drive the loop, the state reset and the arithmetic repeatedly.
diversity_axes.notes: output_budget: whole file 256 B - 64 KiB; at least one track, and at least one track per corpus file carrying more than 512 event bytes; a single meta or sysex payload at most 4 KiB; total text and sysex payload at most 16 KiB. Zero tracks is legal in the format but produces a file that exercises no event code at all, so it is worth at most one outlier file per corpus.
